lines.text: You can start investing with $100. Not $10,000. One hundred dollars. Here's how it works, step by step.
lines.say: You can start investing with a hundred dollars. Not ten thousand. One hundred dollars. Here's how it works, step by step.

lines.text: Quick note: this is education, not advice. We'll explain the options so you can decide.
lines.say: Quick note: this is education, not advice. We'll explain the options so you can decide.

lines.text: Here's the whole path in five steps.
lines.say: Here's the whole path in five steps.

lines.text: Step 1. Get ready.
lines.say: Step one. Get ready.

lines.text: Before investing, many people make sure they have a small emergency fund, so a surprise bill doesn't force them to sell.
lines.say: Before investing, many people make sure they have a small emergency fund, so a surprise bill doesn't force them to sell.

lines.text: And they check their debts. Paying off a card charging 22% is a guaranteed 22% return. Few investments beat that.
lines.say: And they check their debts. Paying off a card charging twenty-two percent is a guaranteed twenty-two percent return. Few investments beat that.

lines.text: Step 2. Pick an account.
lines.say: Step two. Pick an account.

lines.text: You need an account to hold your investments. The two most common for beginners: a regular brokerage account, or a Roth IRA.
lines.say: You need an account to hold your investments. The two most common for beginners: a regular brokerage account, or a Roth IRA.

lines.text: For 2026, you can put up to $7,500 into an IRA, if you have at least that much earned income.
lines.say: For twenty twenty-six, you can put up to seventy-five hundred dollars into an IRA, if you have at least that much earned income.

lines.text: Roth IRAs have income limits, so check the IRS rules for your situation.
lines.say: Roth IRAs have income limits, so check the IRS rules for your situation.

lines.text: Many big brokerages let you open an account with no minimum and charge no commission to buy stocks and funds.
lines.say: Many big brokerages let you open an account with no minimum and charge no commission to buy stocks and funds.

lines.text: SIPC protection covers up to $500,000 if the brokerage itself fails. It does not protect against the market going down.
lines.say: SIPC protection covers up to five hundred thousand dollars if the brokerage itself fails. It does not protect against the market going down.

scene.label: SIPC protection per customer
scene.sub: incl. up to $250K cash; not market losses

lines.text: Step 3. Pick an investment.
lines.say: Step three. Pick an investment.

lines.text: With $100, picking single stocks means betting on just one or two companies.
lines.say: With $100, picking single stocks means betting on just one or two companies.

lines.text: That's why many beginners look at index funds. One fund can hold hundreds of companies at once.
lines.say: That's why many beginners look at index funds. One fund can hold hundreds of companies at once.

lines.text: An S&P 500 index fund, for example, owns pieces of about 500 large U.S. companies.
lines.say: An S and P five hundred index fund, for example, owns pieces of about five hundred large U.S. companies.

lines.text: Watch the fee, called the expense ratio. Some broad index funds charge just a few hundredths of a percent a year.
lines.say: Watch the fee, called the expense ratio. Some broad index funds charge just a few hundredths of a percent a year.

lines.text: Step 4. Buy it.
lines.say: Step four. Buy it.

lines.text: A share of a fund might cost more than $100. That's where fractional shares help: you buy a slice.
lines.say: A share of a fund might cost more than $100. That's where fractional shares help: you buy a slice.

lines.text: You enter a dollar amount, like $100, and the brokerage buys that much of the fund.
lines.say: You enter a dollar amount, like $100, and the brokerage buys that much of the fund.

lines: Get: a slice of the fund

lines.text: Not every brokerage offers fractional shares of every fund, so check before you pick one.
lines.say: Not every brokerage offers fractional shares of every fund, so check before you pick one.

lines.text: Step 5. Keep going.
lines.say: Step five. Keep going.

lines.text: Here's why $100 matters. At an example 7% a year, $100 invested once grows to about $761 in 30 years.
lines.say: Here's why a hundred dollars matters. At an example seven percent a year, a hundred dollars invested once grows to about seven hundred sixty-one dollars in thirty years.

lines.text: But $100 every month at that same rate could grow to about $122,000 in 30 years.
lines.say: But a hundred dollars every month at that same rate could grow to about a hundred and twenty-two thousand dollars in thirty years.

lines.text: You'd have put in $36,000. The rest is growth from compounding.
lines.say: You'd have put in thirty-six thousand dollars. The rest is growth from compounding.

lines.text: That's why many people set up an automatic monthly investment, the same amount every time.
lines.say: That's why many people set up an automatic monthly investment, the same amount every time.

lines.text: Markets go down sometimes, even a lot. Investing can lose money, especially over short periods.
lines.say: Markets go down sometimes, even a lot. Investing can lose money, especially over short periods.

lines.text: So the recap: build a cushion, pick an account, consider a low-cost diversified fund, buy a slice, and keep adding.
lines.say: So the recap: build a cushion, pick an account, consider a low-cost diversified fund, buy a slice, and keep adding.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
lines.say: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: How to Start Investing With $100, Step by Step
post.yt_desc:
You don't need thousands of dollars to start investing. We walk through five steps: building a cushion and checking high-interest debt, choosing between a brokerage account and a Roth IRA (2026 IRA limit: $7,500), what index funds and expense ratios are, buying fractional shares, and why investing a little every month matters, with the math at an example 7% return. Education, not advice.

CHAPTERS

Sources
IRS: 2026 IRA contribution limit ($7,500; $8,600 age 50+), Nov 13, 2025
SIPC: what SIPC protects (up to $500,000, including $250,000 cash)
Federal Reserve G.19: average card APR on accounts assessed interest (22.15%, Q2 2026)
Math: compound growth at an example 7% a year, compounded monthly; not a prediction

News and education, not financial advice. Investing involves risk, including loss of principal.
